design_decision: O9 is the Pareto-knee candidate: it retains continuous 30 mm active BGO while removing the high-Z passive W shell. O10 saves only 8.88 kg more but thins the top active shield to 10 mm and is retained only as a later stress test.

alignment: remove high-Z passive material close to the detector
preserve aperture geometry and segmented detector topology
literature_design_check.open_boundary: native 80 keV versus analysis-level 50 keV active-veto threshold requires a matched-threshold systematic study

physical_changes: BGO side 40 to 30 mm, inner radius fixed at 21.2 cm
BGO bottom 40 to 30 mm, cavity-side z fixed at -19.4 cm
BGO top annulus 40 to 30 mm, cavity-side z fixed at 40.9 cm
remove three 2 mm W mechanical-shell volumes and detector scorers

structural_model_boundary.interpretation: The unchanged outer envelope creates a deliberate service/vacuum gap after BGO thinning. This is a minimal-delta transport model, not a manufacturing or structural qualification.

threshold_boundary.note: C0 and S3d comparisons must freeze the same effective selection. Gehrels' below-50-keV recommendation is not claimed as implemented hardware performance.

unchanged: Al3 and Kapton volume IDs, placements, shapes, materials, and scorers
top service opening, side window, pump-line relief, and NF2 relief scheme
TES/cryostat/BPE/plastic geometry, InstrumentFrame, materials, response, and thresholds
